name: ch02_perplexity_computer
caption: Perplexity Computer running a single task: the agent's cloud sandbox has produced a document that opens in the right-hand side panel.
alt: Perplexity Computer interface with a task list on the left and a generated PDF preview open in a side panel

name: ch02_manus_computer
caption: Manus works the same way: 'Manus's Computer' opens on the right and shows the agent editing a file inside its own per-task machine.
alt: Manus interface with the agent's computer panel open on the right showing a markdown document being written

name: ch04_skills_vs_dependability
caption: The core claim, drawn: as skills, integrations, personality and memory go up (blue arrow), dependability goes down (red arrow).
alt: Whiteboard listing Skills, Integrations, Personality, Memory with a blue up arrow and a red down arrow beside them, and Tasks, Heartbeat, Webhook alongside

name: ch05_seven_to_ten_skills
caption: The rule the presenter lands on, written in red across the sprawling skill map: 7-10 skills per agent.
alt: The skill map with 7-10 skills written in large red handwriting across the bottom

name: ch05_manus_skill_catalogue
caption: Manus's skill catalogue. Skills are added to the command center rather than to a specific agent, which is the design the presenter objects to.
alt: Manus settings modal titled Skills showing a grid of official skills and an Add custom Skills button

name: ch06_intent_tweet
caption: The framing the presenter borrows: Emmett Shear's post about giving models intents, pinned above the dictionary definition of intent - intention or purpose.
alt: Screenshot of a post by Emmett Shear about giving models intents, above a dictionary entry defining in-tent as intention or purpose

name: ch07_telegram_agents
caption: The agents are not hypothetical: a focused agent's skills board sits behind a live Telegram thread where the presenter talks to one of them.
alt: Whiteboard showing a Focused Agent box with Personality, Tasks and Heartbeat cards, overlaid by a Telegram chat window

name: ch07_focused_agent_model
caption: The model in one picture: a focused agent with a personality, tasks and a heartbeat points at three narrow, related goals, and only the skills useful to those goals get added.
alt: Diagram of a Focused Agent with Personality, Tasks, Heartbeat cards, an arrow to a green box of Goal 1, Goal 2, Goal 3 labelled Narrow Related Goals, and a skills box feeding integrations

name: ch08_youtube_agent_full_map
caption: The finished path. Goals - subs, views, conversions - justify three skills (YouTube research, thumbnail generator, control my Notion), which in turn justify exactly four integrations: Serp API, Supadata, Nano Banana and Notion, plus photos of Riley as context.
alt: Completed diagram linking the YouTube AI Agent to goals Subs, Views, Conversions, to three named skills, and to integrations Serp API, Supadata, Nano Banana and Notion

name: ch09_narrow_focus_duplicable
caption: Reason one for narrow focus: a useful agent is duplicable and remixable - a YouTube agent becomes a TikTok or Substack agent with small edits.
alt: Whiteboard heading Narrow Focus with the first bullet Duplicable (Remixable) written beneath it, beside a diagram of agent clusters

name: ch10_sharable_journal_agent
caption: Reason two: sharable. The journal agent lives in Telegram, checks in roughly every 30 minutes, and was handed to a co-founder who reproduced it in about five minutes.
alt: Whiteboard list reading Narrow Focus, Duplicable (Remixable), Sharable, with a Telegram chat window open beside it

name: ch10_agent_team_clusters
caption: The team the journal feeds. The journal agent and the email newsletter agent sit in different clusters and keep their own goals; only the journal itself crosses between them.
alt: Diagram of agent clusters showing a Marketing and Distribution row with Email Newsletter Agent and a Content Creation row with YouTube Agent and Journal Agent highlighted

name: ch12_six_reasons_and_team
caption: The complete argument on one board: narrow focus makes agents duplicable, sharable, understandable, reviewable, easier to loop and more autonomous - and the right-hand diagram is the team those agents would form.
alt: Whiteboard listing Narrow Focus with six benefits beside a diagram of three clusters of named agents

name: ch12_open_questions
caption: The three unanswered questions the presenter says future videos will tackle: running agents efficiently in the cloud, sharing them with a team, and letting them communicate with one another.
alt: Whiteboard with three handwritten blue questions about running agents in the cloud, sharing them with the team, and getting them to communicate with one another
